item.title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
item.description: President Trump forced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia after his 11-day ouster following allegations of ties to a Chinese intelligence asset. Despite warnings from intelligence agencies, Trump cited stock market stabilization as his primary motivation, sparking intense scrutiny in Washington over the intersection of critical tech leadership and national security.

item.title: SpaceX-Tesla: the directors negotiating the biggest merger ever
item.description: SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to negotiate a potential $3.5 trillion all-stock merger. The companies have retained Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Evercore to advise on valuation and exchange ratios, with the objective of creating a global mega-corporation while ensuring CEO Elon Musk is excluded from the governance and approval process.

item.title: Xiaomi’s Sales Slip After Memory Shortages Weigh on Smartphones
item.description: Xiaomi Corp. reported a Q3 revenue of 107.2 billion yuan, down 5.2% YoY, with net income plunging 68% to 3.9 billion yuan. Driven by AI’s aggressive consumption of memory chips, supply shortages have forced the company to curtail low-end device production and shift focus to premium segments, including the Xiaomi 18 Fold and SkyNomad SUVs, to stabilize flagging shipments.

item.title: OpenRouter removes Together AI, Phala, and Novita over data policy violations; Novita says a misconfiguration sent some MiniMax requests to MiniMax official API (Bill Toulas/BleepingComputer)
item.description: OpenRouter has removed Together AI, Phala, and Novita from its platform due to data policy violations. Novita acknowledged that a technical misconfiguration caused certain user requests intended for their service to be inadvertently routed to the official MiniMax API endpoints.

item.title: Bloomberg Asia
item.description: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming is now Asia’s richest person, with an estimated fortune of more than $105bn, putting him ahead of Indian industrialist Gautam Adani, according to Bloomberg. The ranking comes from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, and Zhang, 43, has never held the top spot before. The figure is an estimate, and other trackers disagree. item.title: AWS debuts Strands Decider v2, a family of five open decision models based on Google's Gemma 4, ranging from 2B to 31B parameters, under the Apache 2.0 license (Frederic Lardinois/The New Stack)
item.description: Amazon has launched the Strands Decider v2 model family, featuring five decision-making models based on Google's Gemma 4 architecture, ranging from 2B to 31B parameters. All models are released under the Apache 2.0 license to facilitate customized enterprise decision-making tasks.

item.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
item.description: Cisco's VP of Engineering and Security CTO Thomas Graf has partnered with OpenAI to launch the 'Secure Infrastructure Project,' featuring an open-source tool called Shirudo that utilizes immutable architecture and reinforcement learning for proactive defense. This initiative addresses the critical threat where AI-driven vulnerability exploitation precedes public disclosure, shifting security from reactive patching to resilient, design-based protection.

item.title: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians
item.description: Google Maps has failed to annotate over 900 checkpoints and movement restrictions in the West Bank, creating significant safety risks for Palestinian drivers. Despite internal awareness and technical capability to implement such features, Google has neglected to integrate real-time hazard data, forcing users to rely on makeshift third-party reporting channels for navigation safety.

item.title: ChatGPT expands GPT-6.2 Sol as OpenAI sets retirement date for two models
item.description: OpenAI has deployed the GPT-6.2 Sol model across all subscription tiers, featuring enhanced multimodal recognition and cross-application task execution. Simultaneously, the company scheduled the retirement of GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra for December 23, aiming to accelerate the streamlining of its model ecosystem.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is a White House Scandal
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, triggering market instability. President Donald Trump has intervened, with Attorney General Todd Blanche confirming that Huang is not currently a target of DOJ investigations, aimed at stabilizing the AI supply chain and capital market sentiment.

item.title: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say
item.description: Federal prosecutors disclosed in court filings that former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan used OpenAI’s Codex AI tool to configure recording devices, capturing dozens of confidential meetings, including sensitive discussions with a foreign government. While data exfiltration remains under investigation, the act constitutes a significant breach of trade secrets and attorney-client privilege.

item.title: OpenAI Staffer Likely Captured Secrets on Hidden Bug, US Says
item.description: Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan is accused of planting recording devices in executive conference rooms, capturing hundreds of audio files including sovereign government briefings and confidential customer data. Prosecutors allege he utilized OpenAI’s internal tool, Codex, to configure the devices for voice-activated recording and automated exfiltration, with judicial proceedings now underway.

item.title: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges
item.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot officially attributed the cyberattack on over 700 European supermarket refrigeration controllers to Iran's 'SHAHID KAVEH' cyber unit during a G7 meeting. The attack, occurring between October 11-12, caused widespread equipment failures, fires, and tens of millions of euros in food losses, marking a transition from espionage to physical infrastructure sabotage.

item.description: French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. item.title: Australian IoT Startup Aims to Help Bridge the Gap Between AI and the Real World
item.description: Australian satellite IoT provider Myriota has secured approximately $40 million in the first close of its Series C funding round to scale its proprietary satellite constellation and expand its workforce. The company specializes in low-power, wide-area connectivity for industrial data collection in remote environments.

item.title: HPE Gives Outlook That Falls Short of Optimistic Estimates
item.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $14.5 billion, a 50% year-over-year increase, beating analyst estimates of $14.3 billion. Despite the strong headline figures, the company's Q1 revenue guidance fell short of the most optimistic analyst expectations, triggering a 6%+ decline in after-hours trading due to concerns over the sustainability of high-growth AI server demand.
